newsitem.title: USA: Latin debts mixed, Mexico economic plan gets shrug.
newsitem.headline: Latin debts mixed, Mexico economic plan gets shrug.

text.p: Constrained by the range-bound U.S. Treasuries, emerging market bonds ignored country-specific news to trade lightly mixed, traders said.

An economic development plan for Mexico delivered by President Ernesto Zedillo and Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz on Tuesday was greeted with enthusiasm in the equities market, but barely made a ripple in fixed income instruments.
The plan, which set development goals into the year 2000, emphasized private investment and public savings to spur economic growth, while relegating private consumption to a secondary role.
"It is a realistic program," said Walter Molano, director of Latin America economic research at SBC/Warburg.
Inflation is projected to remain in double-digits and the ratio of savings to gross domestic product to rise slowly.
Uncharacteristic in an election year, the plan refrained from appealing to voters with promises of government largess on public spending, he noted.
Javier Murcio, Latin America economist at CS First Boston, agreed that the macroeconomic plan was not made to woo votes.
"They know that any grandiose plan would likely backfire," he said.
The gradual decline in inflation and moderate growth envisioned in the plan should be positive for fixed income investors, Murcio added.
Mexico Par bonds MX625L19=RR were unchanged at 75-5/8 bid and the UMS 26 global bond was bid a smidgen 1/8 higher at 111-5/8.
Brazil bonds also hovered around late Monday's levels as investors made minor adjustments before the expiration of the exchange offer on Tuesday.

It has been widely expected that the new 30-year global bond would be heavily over-subscribed, although it was unclear how many Brady bonds would be tendered in exchange as the offer also allowed investors to bid for the bonds outright.

"It would make more sense to buy the bonds outright," said a trader, noting that the Par, the Discount and the C bonds were trading signficantly above the established exchange prices. "But the catch is that you might be left out without a swap."
The Brazilian government put a 25 percent cap on the amount of winning cash tenders.
Reaction to Brazil's $271 million May trade deficit, reported on Tuesday, was muted.

Although the trade gap narrowed signficantly from the monthly levels reported in March and April, some traders dismissed the improvement as seasonal phenomenon due to post-harvest agricultural exports.
"We've heard from some estimates that (the gap) could be as low as $100 (million) to $150 million," said a trader.

In the broader market, Polish debt papers firmed as Standard and Poor's affirmed the bound's BBB-minus foreign currency and A-minus local currency debt rating, while revising the outlook to positive from stable on both.
Poland Par bonds PO275024=RR added 1/4 to 55-7/8 bid and PDI bonds PO325024=RR gained 5/8 to 84-3/8 bid.
